recent_posts.title: Fast and Comprehensive Code Review, Now in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: Windsurf now integrates two AI-powered code review tools: Devin Review and Quick Review. Devin Review organizes PR diffs by logic rather than file order, groups related edits, identifies bugs with explanations, and supports an Autofix workflow where Devin can generate and apply fixes directly. Quick Review is a faster local tool powered by SWE-check, a specialized bug detection model claimed to be up to 10x faster than a deep review agent, usable before opening a PR. Both tools are available in Windsurf 2.0 today.

recent_posts.title: Windsurf 2.0: Introducing the Agent Command Center and Devin in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: Windsurf 2.0 introduces the Agent Command Center, a Kanban-style interface for managing multiple local and cloud agents simultaneously within the IDE. A new organizational unit called Spaces groups agent sessions, PRs, files, and context by task or project. The release also integrates Devin, an autonomous cloud-based software engineering agent, directly into Windsurf. Devin runs in its own VM, handles complex end-to-end tasks like debugging, deployment, and testing, and is included with every Windsurf plan. The goal is to unify planning, delegation, and code review in a single editor workflow.

recent_posts.title: GPT-5.4 is now available in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: GPT-5.4 is now available in Windsurf, the AI coding assistant, with five reasoning effort levels ranging from No Reasoning to Extra High Reasoning. Promotional pricing for self-serve users starts at 1x credits for No and Low Reasoning tiers, scaling up to 8x credits for Extra High Reasoning. The model is accessible to Pro, Teams, Enterprise, and Trial users.

recent_posts.title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 is now available in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: Claude Sonnet 4.6 is now integrated into Windsurf, an AI-powered code editor. Self-serve users get promotional pricing with 2x credits for standard mode and 3x credits when using thinking mode for a limited time.

recent_posts.title: GLM-5 and Minimax M2.5 are now available in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: Windsurf now supports two new AI models: GLM-5 from Zhipu AI (0.75x credits) and Minimax M2.5 (0.25x credits), both with limited-time promotional pricing. The models are available to all users and included in Arena Mode's Frontier Arena and Hybrid Arena battle groups for head-to-head comparisons.

recent_posts.title: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark is now available in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI's GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark model is now available in Windsurf through Arena Mode's Fast Arena and Hybrid Arena battle groups. The model is optimized for real-time coding and is exclusively accessible through these arena battle groups rather than the regular model selector.

recent_posts.title: Windsurf Arena Mode Leaderboard: The People Want Speed
recent_posts.summary: Windsurf releases Arena Mode leaderboard results showing surprising rankings where speed matters as much as quality. Unlike traditional web-based arenas, this in-IDE evaluation allows users to vote for faster models if they complete first with good-enough results. Key findings include Gemini 3 Flash and Grok Code Fast beating Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Haiku 4.5 beating GPT 5.2, and Windsurf's own SWE 1.5 outperforming Claude Haiku. The methodology penalizes inefficient thinking tokens and reflects real-world IDE usage patterns across 40,000 votes, with no model achieving over 80% win rate.

recent_posts.title: Opus 4.6 (fast mode) is now available in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: Claude Opus 4.6 (fast mode) is now available in Windsurf with promotional pricing until February 16. The fast mode offers the same intelligence as standard Opus 4.6 but delivers up to 2.5x higher output speeds. Self-serve users get 10x credits without thinking mode and 12x credits with thinking mode during the promotional period.

recent_posts.title: Opus 4.6 is now available in Windsurf
recent_posts.summary: Claude Opus 4.6 is now available in Windsurf with promotional pricing of 2x credits without thinking mode and 3x credits with thinking mode. The model can be tested in Arena Mode's Frontier Arena alongside other frontier models. According to Windsurf's CEO, Opus 4.6 shows improvements over 4.5, particularly for debugging and exploring unfamiliar codebases, with longer thinking times that benefit tasks requiring deeper reasoning.
